data.title: Jim Cramer Trims Broadcom, Palo Alto Networks, Adds BNY, Kimberly-Clark and Micron
data.description:
According to CNBC, Jim Cramer’s portfolio reduced exposure to some artificial intelligence winners last week, including trimming Palo Alto Networks ahead of earnings and exiting Corning, while adding BNY, Kimberly-Clark and Micron. The moves came as the S&P 500 rose 0.1% for the week and the Nasdaq gained 0.4%, with both indexes posting their fifth weekly advance in six weeks.

Broadcom remained under pressure despite better-than-expected revenue and earnings. CEO Hock Tan raised his fiscal 2027 AI revenue forecast to $115 billion and said it is expected to double to $230 billion in fiscal 2028. Cramer also said he sold half of the remaining Broadcom position before earnings and is willing to keep the rest because of the company’s relationship with AI startup Anthropic.

Palo Alto Networks reported strong results after Tuesday’s close, and Cramer said AI remains a major tailwind for cybersecurity. He said roughly $1 trillion of global cybersecurity infrastructure needs to be modernized and noted that the stock fell more than 10% last week after profit-taking. Nvidia also rose 6% last week after its $12.9 billion acquisition of Hugging Face, which Cramer said deepens the ecosystem around its chips and gives it access to an open-source AI platform used by more than 18 million developers.

data.title: XDOF Nears Late-Stage Funding Round at $1.2 Billion Valuation
data.description:
XDOF is in late-stage talks for a Series B financing round that could value the robotics data startup at about $1.2 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. According to ChainCatcher, 8VC is leading the round, though the final terms have not been set and could still change.

The company was founded in 2024 by University of California, Berkeley researchers Philipp Wu, who is CEO, and Fred Shentu, who is CTO. XDOF collects real-world teleoperation data to train general-purpose robots.

XDOF previously raised $70 million in Series A funding from investors including Thrive Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Lux, and Spark Capital. The company had not planned to raise again so soon, but people familiar with the matter said rapid business growth and annualized revenue approaching $50 million drew interest from multiple venture firms.

The exact size of the new round was not disclosed, and it was not confirmed whether the reported $1.2 billion valuation includes the new capital.

data.title: Fed Hike Odds Rise After Strong US Jobs Report
data.description:
Seaport Research Partners Managing Director and Chief Equity Strategist Jonathan Golub said a stronger-than-expected US jobs report reinforces the case for the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, despite US President Donald Trump’s calls for lower borrowing costs, according to Bloomberg.

Golub also told Bloomberg This Weekend hosts Christina Ruffini and Jeff Mason that his bigger concern is longer-term bond yields as heavy AI investment and government borrowing compete for capital.

data.title: BloFin Says Bitcoin Debasement Trade Has Entered Second Phase
data.description: BloFin says Bitcoin’s debasement trade has entered a “second phase” as US federal debt tops $40 trillion and investors watch efforts to control borrowing costs. Bitcoin is trading near $80,000, about 37% below last year’s record high, even as the government runs a deficit close to 6% of GDP and long-term borrowing costs stay elevated, according to BeInCrypto, which cites BloFin Research. The report says Treasury buybacks and rising yields may be shaping expectations more than money creation itself.

data.title: UK Maritime Agency Reports Multiple Merchant Ships Hit in Arabian Gulf and Gulf of Oman
data.description: According to Sina Finance, the UK Maritime Trade Operations office received reports that multiple merchant ships in the northern Arabian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman were hit by firepower capable of disabling vessels as part of ongoing military activity in the region. The office said it could not yet confirm whether there were any casualties or environmental damage.

data.title: AI TRENDS | OpenAI Astra Technology Raises Safety Concerns
data.description:
OpenAI said its upcoming Astra model has upgraded capabilities in code writing and operating desktop applications. According to Sina Finance, a person familiar with Astra's development said an innovation designed to improve model performance would cause Astra and similar models to reveal less of their "thought process," making it harder to monitor and identify bad behavior.

According to Sina Finance, while the flaw may not be a major issue for Astra itself, the technology has raised concerns inside OpenAI and across the industry that if AI developers adopt and greatly strengthen it, it may become difficult to prevent rogue AI from breaching company systems, including those at OpenAI and Hugging Face.

data.title: Google Fixes Chrome Zero-Day CVE-2026-85046 After Active Exploitation
data.description:
Google has patched a high-severity Chrome vulnerability, CVE-2026-85046, after confirming it was exploited in the wild. According to ChainCatcher, the flaw was found in the V8 engine used to run JavaScript and WebAssembly, and Google did not disclose the attacker, target, or exact exploitation method.

The fix is included in Chrome versions 152.7977.82 and 152.7977.83 and will roll out over the next few days or weeks. The vulnerability was reported by security researcher Salvatore Gulizia on August 4, who received a $1,000 bug bounty. The update includes 12 security fixes in total, including nine high-severity issues and two medium-severity issues. Google has not linked the flaw to any crypto asset theft, although browser wallets, exchange accounts, and trading extensions have previously been targeted through other methods.

data.title: Walmart To Expand Dunkin' Delivery Through Walmart Restaurant Delivery
data.description: According to CNBC, Walmart will begin delivering Dunkin' products from its own stores and then expand the program over the next year to include most of Dunkin's roughly 10,000 U.S. locations, many of which are outside Walmart stores. The retailer said the service will run through Walmart Restaurant Delivery, which first launched with Subway, and a Walmart spokesperson said the move is meant to add convenience while pairing restaurant delivery with Walmart's product assortment. Walmart senior vice president Greg Cathey said nearly 65% of restaurant orders since the Subway launch were delivered with items customers needed quickly from Walmart, one in five combined orders were from first-time Express Delivery users, and nearly 30% of those customers returned within 30 days. Walmart CFO John David Rainey said customers want value, convenience and speed, and the company said U.S. fast delivery under 30 minutes grew 48% in the quarter.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Esper Warns Pentagon Polygraph Probe May Hurt Officer Corps
data.description:
Former Defense Secretary Mark Esper called the Pentagon’s polygraph testing of roughly 50 Joint Staff members unprecedented in scale, according to Bloomberg.

He told hosts Christina Ruffini and Jeff Mason that he is less worried about immediate combat readiness than the institutional impact of leadership turnover and its possible effect on the military’s tradition of an apolitical officer corps as officials investigate leaks about US munitions stocks.
